o1.biggest_strength: It builds bundle one on the top face wash + serum pair at a modest ₹869. Every profit figure includes RTO cost (₹130 × 40% COD × band rate) as well as the ₹70 shipping, and each bundle and the ₹599 line get clear break-even points.
o1.biggest_mistake: It never treats COD differently: there is no COD fee, no higher COD bar and no prepaid-only free shipping, even though under-₹500 COD orders are refused 29% of the time. The lip balm is not used as a cart add-on to cross the threshold.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add a COD-specific rule (a COD fee or a higher free-shipping bar for COD) with the RTO saving worked out, and make the lip balm a cart add-on that lifts ₹400–599 carts over the line.

o2.biggest_strength: The price ladder on the serum page (₹599 → ₹749 → ₹999) is smart, and the case against simply discounting the 1,033 pair orders a month the store already gets is thoughtful.
o2.biggest_mistake: Its core profit maths leaves out RTO cost. The threshold sizing assumes only 6% of orders fall between ₹499 and ₹598, when an even spread of the 27% band from ₹500 to ₹699 gives about 13%, and that clashes with its own ₹699 figure. The add/pay/walk shares are made up, so the ₹3.4 lakh a year claim is shaky.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Put RTO into every profit line, size the affected orders consistently from the band data, handle COD separately, and keep the lip balm as an add-on instead of a discounted main bundle.

reason: Output 1 puts my best pair first at a sensible price, counts refused COD orders in every rupee and keeps its threshold maths consistent. Output 2 has nice ideas, but its threshold numbers don't hold together and it drops RTO from the profit maths.
